summary: OWASP review of the MENU editor focused on XSS via author-entered button labels/URLs and the End-sentinel encoding. No v-html anywhere; all labels/urls render via Vue text interpolation or bind to inputs. URL scheme is mirrored client-side and strictly enforced server-side (Decision 10). No secrets, no new network surface.

findings.finding: Button labels and URLs are author-entered. They are rendered exclusively through {{ }} interpolation / v-model-bound inputs — confirmed no v-html in components/funnels or pages/projects (grep clean; only a documenting comment references v-html).
findings.resolution: No change — XSS-safe by default interpolation as required.

findings.finding: URL buttons validated client-side with /^https?:\/\//i (UX mirror). The authoritative SSRF/scheme-injection defense (strict URI parse, exact http/https scheme, non-empty host, whitespace reject) is server-side in FunnelService.requireHttpUrl. Client check is a UX proxy only, consistent with the existing IMAGE_URL_RE idiom.
findings.resolution: No change — defense-in-depth, server is authoritative.

findings.finding: End target encoded strictly as targetStepId:null (never empty string), preventing a spurious non-null id that would otherwise trip server 422 funnel_broken_edge. Verified by the 'End encoded as null' unit test.
